title: Fractal Dimension Index (FDI)
summary: A fractal dimension of the last 30 closes built on Carlos Sevcik's method: lower for a clean trend, higher for a choppy range, with 1.5 between them.
description:
The Fractal Dimension Index estimates how jagged the recent price path is, using the waveform method published by Carlos Sevcik. The last `length` values of the source (30 closes by default) are mapped onto a unit square: time runs from 0 to 1 in equal steps, and price is rescaled so the window's lowest value is 0 and its highest is 1.

The study then adds up the lengths of the straight segments that join the rescaled points into a total path length `L`, and computes `FDI = 1 + (ln L + ln 2) / ln(2 * (length - 1))`. Sevcik's own estimate is `1 + ln L / ln(2 * (length - 1))`; the index adds `ln 2` to it, which lifts every reading by the same amount (about 0.17 with 30 bars) so that a path zigzagging across the whole range on every bar reads exactly 2 and a random walk reads about 1.5. A straight path gives the lowest values (about 1.26 with a 30 bar window, closer to 1 as the window grows). A window with no range at all is treated as a flat path of length 1.
howToRead:
Values below 1.5 mean price has been moving in a fairly direct line, the mark of a trend, and the lower the value the cleaner the trend. Values above 1.5 mean the path has been doubling back on itself, the mark of a range or a noisy market. The index says nothing about direction: a steady fall and a steady rise both read low.

Traders use it as a filter: trend-following rules when the index is falling or below 1.5, range rules when it is above. A move from high readings to low ones often marks a breakout from congestion. Readings depend on the window length, and short windows give a noisy line.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The price series whose path is measured. Close is the usual choice.

settings.label: Length
settings.description: Bars in the window. 30 is the usual value; a longer window gives a smoother, slower index.

faq.q: Does a low value mean price is going up?
faq.a: No. A low value means price has moved in a fairly straight line in either direction. Use the price chart or a trend study for the direction.

A random walk has a fractal dimension of 1.5, and with the ln 2 term the index reads close to 1.5 on a random walk at the usual window lengths. Below it the path is smoother than chance, which suggests a trend; above it the path is more jagged than chance, which suggests mean reversion.

faq.q: Why does a perfect trend not read exactly 1?
faq.a: The index approaches the true dimension only as the window grows, and its ln 2 term lifts every reading. With 30 bars a straight line reads about 1.26 and a perfectly flat window about 1.17, so judge readings against 1.5 and against their own recent history rather than against 1.
